Targeted strategies that address the needs of alcohol or nicotine using women and that can reduce the risk of unintended pregnancy may be beneficial.

title: Prospective florbetapir f 18 pet/ct to evaluate perfusion patterns and amyloid deposition in chronic temporal lobe epilepsy
abstract: Rationale: The long term effects of chronic temporal lobe epilepsy (TLE) on memory and cognition are incompletely understood. There are progressive global and regional changes in brain structure and function in patients with TLE which are similar to pathophysiological changes in Alzheimer's disease, including senile plaque deposition. (Mackenzie IR, Miller LA. Senile plaques in temporal lobe epilepsy. Acta Neuropathol (Berl) 1994;87:504-10., Noebels J. A perfect storm: Converging paths of epilepsy and Alzheimer's dementia intersect in the hippocampal formation. Epilepsia 2011;52 Suppl 1:39-4) Florbetapir PET/CT imaging is a relatively new FDAapproved imaging technique that provides the ability to detect the presence and location of amyloid in the brain. We chose to use this technology to investigate perfusion patterns of dynamic uptake as well as amyloid deposition in the whole brain of patients with chronic TLE. We report preliminary findings showing perfusion changes. Methods: We plan to recruit ten subjects with chronic TLE. To be included, a subject should be at least twenty years old, have had epilepsy for at least 20 years, and have EEG and MRI findings which support TLE. Subjects who have already undergone epilepsy surgery, have a history of a significant head trauma or chronic alcohol abuse, have another significant neurological disorder other than epilepsy, women who were pregnant or breastfeeding, and those found to be apolipoprotein E4 homozygotes were excluded. Well-selected subjects underwent a 60 minute dynamic PET/CT scan starting immediately after intravenous injection of Florbetapir with the following framing sequence: 4 x 15 seconds, 4 x 30 seconds, 3 x 60 seconds, 3 x 120 seconds, 2 x 240 seconds, 8 x 5 minutes. Initial perfusion patterns were qualitatively assessed by a blinded neuroradiologist (JM) trained to clinically interpret Florbetapir imaging. Perfusion patterns were correlated with EEG and MRI data to assess for concordance of localizing findings. Results: Three subjects have completed the study. Qualitative comparison of sequentially-timed dynamic uptake images following Florbetapir injection revealed temporal hypoperfusion ipsilateral to the epileptogenic side within the first 1-2 minutes of the scan in two out of three cases. The third case revealed no lateralized perfusion pattern. Conclusions: Preliminary data analysis suggests that dynamic Florbetapir PET/CT started immediately after injection may reveal similar hypoperfusion patterns compared to other functional imaging modalities used in the evaluation of TLE. Initial changes in perfusion seen with Florbetapir PET/CT may be an important factor in quantitative analysis of amyloid deposition and interpretation of results.

title: 66th Annual National Conference of the Indian Psychiatric Society, ANCIPS 2014
abstract: The proceedings contain 373 papers. The topics discussed include: ondine curse: a severe presentation of obsessive compulsive disorder; executive cognitive dysfunction in alcohol dependence: a case control study from a tertiary care center; a case report of petrol dependence with comorbid ADHD: is there a bidirectional relationship?; depression and quality of life in key caregivers of dementia; a study to correlate the neuropsychiatric manifestations of dementia with the MRI-based hippocampal volume; spectrum of behavioral abnormalities in patients with CNS infections, meningitis, and encephalitis; associations between life events and the suicide intent of first episode of deliberate self-harm; prevalence and associated risk factors of postpartum depression in women attending rural hospital; a study of relationship between duration of first hospital stay and readmission rate in a psychiatric unit of teaching hospital; and premenstrual syndrome: prevalence, phenomenology, and personality factors in college going girl students.

title: Family psychosocial characteristics, tobacco, alcohol, and other drug use, and teenage pregnancy
abstract: The aim of this study was to analyze associations between demographic factors, family psychosocial characteristics, tobacco, alcohol, and other drug use, and adolescent motherhood. This was a case-control study in Porto Alegre, Rio Grande do Sul State, Brazil, with 431 adolescents 14 to 16 years of age who gave birth in 2009 (cases) and 862 adolescents who had never given birth (controls). Three-stage hierarchical logistic regression was performed (demographic, family psychosocial, and lifestyle variables). Lower economic class, not having lived with the parents from 10 to 14 years of age (OR = 1.67; 95%CI: 1.12-2.48), having taken care of other children (OR = 1.42; 95%CI: 1.09-1.87), siblings who had children before 20 years of age (OR = 1.56; 95%CI: 1.19- 2.06), having tried smoking (OR = 1.94; 95%CI: 1.35-2.78), and having arrived home intoxicated (OR = 1.67; 95%CI: 1.12-2.48) were associated with adolescent motherhood. Greater attention should be given to family relations in association with tobacco and alcohol consumption, since the use of these substances is associated with adolescent motherhood.

title: Single- and Multiple-Dose Pharmacokinetic, Safety, and Tolerability Profiles of Olanzapine Long-Acting Injection: An Open-Label, Multicenter, Nonrandomized Study in Patients With Schizophrenia
abstract: Background: This was the first study, to our knowledge, in patients with schizophrenia in which olanzapine long-acting injection (LAI) was used to attempt delivery of depot formulation in multiple therapeutic doses. Objective: This study assessed the safety profile, tolerability, and pharmacokinetic (PK) properties of olanzapine after single and multiple administrations of olanzapine LAI and evaluated maintenance of symptom control. Methods: This was an open-label, multicenter, nonrandomized study of olanzapine LAI in patients with schizophrenia stabilized with oral olanzapine. Key inclusion criteria included well-tolerated and efficacious treatment with daily olanzapine. Patients were required to be receiving a stable oral dose for 4weeks before study entry with no requirement for as-needed additional antipsychotic medication within 2weeks before entry. Exclusion criteria included serious unstable illnesses, unresolved seizures, pregnancy or breastfeeding, hypothyroidism, hyperthyroidism, narrow-angle glaucoma, or serious suicidal risk. Initially, 34 patients received olanzapine LAI as a single injection of 50 to 450 mg, and as the study progressed, 247 patients received consecutive injections of 100 to 405 mg olanzapine LAI administered every 2, 3, or 4 weeks for 3 to 6 months. Spontaneously reported adverse events were recorded at each visit. Analyses of efficacy and safety profile parameters were performed on an intent-to-treat basis. All hypotheses were tested at a 2-sided significance level of P < 0.05. Results: Study participants had a mean age of 39 years and were primarily white men. The PK properties suggested prolonged release providing sustained olanzapine plasma concentrations and supporting a dosing interval ≤4 weeks. Olanzapine LAI doses of 150 or 300mg every 2weeks and 210 or 405mg every 4weeks provide mean steady-state olanzapine concentrations similar to those after oral administration of 5 to 20mg/d. The mean baseline Brief Psychiatric Rating Scale score of 17.27 decreased by 2.68 points, and the mean baseline Clinical Global Impression-Severity score of 3.39 decreased by 0.23 points, indicating that patients' psychiatric health was maintained or slightly improved. Significant mean weight gain (P < 0.001) and treatment-emergent changes in nonfasting glucose were observed. Incidence of weight gain ≥7% of baseline was observed in 17.8% of patients. The common adverse events were injection site pain, anxiety, sedation, insomnia, somnolence, and headache, and the safety profile for olanzapine LAI was comparable to that of oral olanzapine, except for injection site-related adverse events. Conclusion: The safety profile and PK data from this study support continued clinical development of olanzapine LAI in controlled efficacy studies at doses ≤300 mg every 2 weeks or 405 mg every 4 weeks. Clinical trial registry ID: 4535 http://www.lillytrials.com/results/ZyprexaLAI.pdf. © 2013 Elsevier HS Journals, Inc.

title: Light drinking versus abstinence in pregnancy - Behavioural and cognitive outcomes in 7-year-old children: A longitudinal cohort study
abstract: Objective To assess whether light drinking in pregnancy is linked to unfavourable developmental outcomes in children. Design Prospective population-based cohort. Setting UK. Population Ten thousand five hundred and thirty-four 7-year-olds. Methods Quasi-experimental using propensity score matching (PSM) to compare children born to light (up to 2 units per week) and non-drinkers. Main outcome measures Behavioural difficulties rated by parents and teachers; cognitive test scores for reading, maths and spatial skills. Results Ordinary least squares (OLS) regression and PSM analyses are presented. For behavioural difficulties, unadjusted estimates for percentage standard deviation (SD) score differences ranged from 2 to 14%. On adjustment for potential confounders, differences were attenuated, with a loss of statistical significance, except for teacher-rated boys' difficulties. For boys, parent-rated behavioural difficulties: unadjusted, -11.5; OLS, -4.3; PSM, -6.8; teacher-rated behavioural difficulties: unadjusted, -13.9; OLS, -9.6; PSM, -10.8. For girls, parent-rated behavioural difficulties: unadjusted, -9.6; OLS, -2.9; PSM, -4.5; teacher-rated behavioural difficulties: unadjusted, -2.4; OLS, 4.9; PSM, 3.9. For cognitive test scores, unadjusted estimates for differences ranged between 12 and 21% of an SD score for reading, maths and spatial skills. After adjustment for potential confounders, estimates were reduced, but remained statistically significantly different for reading and for spatial skills in boys. For boys, reading: unadjusted, 20.9; OLS, 8.3; PSM, 7.3; maths: unadjusted, 14.7; OLS, 5.0; PSM, 6.5; spatial skills: unadjusted, 16.2; OLS, 7.6; PSM, 8.1. For girls, reading: unadjusted, 11.6; OLS, -0.3; PSM, -0.5; maths: unadjusted, 12.9; OLS, 4.3; PSM, 3.9; spatial skills: unadjusted, 16.2; OLS, 7.7; PSM, 6.4. Conclusion The findings suggest that light drinking during pregnancy is not linked to developmental problems in mid-childhood. These findings support current UK Department of Health guidelines on drinking during pregnancy. © 2013 The Authors BJOG An International Journal of Obstetrics and Gynaecology © 2013 RCOG.

title: Predictors of antenatal alcohol use among Australian women: A prospective cohort study
abstract: Objective To identify predictors of antenatal alcohol consumption among women who usually consume alcohol. Design Prospective cohort study. Setting Australian Longitudinal Study on Women's Health (ALSWH). Population or Sample A total of 1969 women sampled from the ALSWH 1973-78 cohort. Methods Women were included if they were pregnant in 2000, 2003, 2006 or 2009. The relationship between antenatal alcohol consumption and sociodemographics, reproductive health, mental health, physical health, health behaviours, alcohol guidelines and healthcare factors was investigated using a multivariate logistic regression model. Main outcome measures Alcohol use during pregnancy. Results Most (82.0%) women continued to drink alcohol during pregnancy. Women were more likely to drink alcohol during pregnancy if they had consumed alcohol on a weekly basis before pregnancy (odds ratio [OR] 1.47; 95% confidence interval [95% CI] 1.13-1.90), binge drank before pregnancy (OR 2.28; 95% CI 1.76-2.94), or if they were pregnant while alcohol guidelines recommended low alcohol versus abstinence (OR 1.60; 95% CI 1.26-2.03). Drinking during pregnancy was less likely if women had a Health Care Card (OR 0.63; 95% CI 0.45-0.88) or if they had ever had fertility problems (OR 0.64; 95% CI 0.48-0.86). Conclusions Most Australian women who drank alcohol continued to do so during pregnancy. Prepregnancy alcohol consumption was one of the main predictors of antenatal alcohol use. Alcohol guidelines, fertility problems and Health Care Card status also impacted antenatal alcohol consumption. © 2013 RCOG.

title: Efficacy of antidepressants in the treatment of major depressive disorder: A naturalistic study
abstract: Objective: This is a prospective, naturalistic study to determine the type of treatment offered to depressive out-patients in a psychiatric clinic, antidepressants (AD) most frequently used, their effectiveness, and variables involved in a better response. Method: 302, out of 3.042 patients, met DSMIV-R criteria for a Major depressive disorder, females: 165 (64.6%), with a mean age of 56.5 years (22-87 y). Clinical data obtained from their clinical history records. Of all patients, 88% were referred from GP settings, only 12% from hospital emergencies. 55.9% had a diagnostic of moderate to severe first episode, 44% had a recurrent one. Severity CGI-S >3. Visits were performed monthly during the first trimester, then every 2 months. Follow-up duration was 22 weeks. The output was evaluated with the Clinical Global Impression- Improvement Scale (CGI-I), the functional recovery with the Global Assessment of Functioning (GAF). CGI-I = 1 and GAF>90 was considered remission; CGI-I between 2 and 3, with GAF 81-90 a partial response. Student's t test used for continuous variables; Chi-square test for discrete variables. Results: Of the 302 patients, 246 received only pharmacological treatment (81.4%), and 18% were referred also with a psychologist. Venlafaxine XR was the AD more frequently prescribed (35.1%), SSRIs 45.4%, Tryciclics 5.3%, Other AD (Agomelatine, Duloxetine, Mirtazapine, Bupropion) 6%, and a combination of AD 8.3%. Most of the patients (79.8%) had no other psychiatric conditions, 14.6% had an Axis II disorder (cluster C), 2.6% anxiety disorder, and 2.6% alcohol abuse disorder. Patients with an anxiety or personality disorder were treated more often with psychotherapy than the rest (30% vs. 16%) Chi-square 6.085 df 1 p = 0.014 After a follow-up of 22 weeks, most patients had a remission (68.9%), 76 patients (25%) had only a partial response. 18 patients did not report any improvement. Median time to maximum response obtained was 7.95 weeks. Variables influencing in a better outcome were absence of comorbidity (Chi-square 15.895 df 2 p <0.001) and type of antidepressant used: optimal responses were obtained with SSRIs, Venlafaxine-XR and Tryciclics. SSRIs vs. other AD p<0.05; SSRIs vs. combination of AD p<0.001; Venlafaxine-XR vs. combination of AD: p <0.05. The average response time was lower with SSRIs than a combination of AD (p = 0.001) or other AD (p<0.05) Discussion: A high rate of remission was obtained, probably due to the poor comorbidity in the sample. Several authors have described it as a factor of worst prognosis [1,2]. The apparent ineffectiveness of adjuvant psychotherapy may be related to the higher frequency of comorbidity found in patients who were referred to a psychologist. Escitalopram, considered the best SSRI [3] was prescribed in the 26.4% of the patients with SSRIs drugs, but in our study Escitalopram did no show significant superiority in efficacy compared with other SSRIs. A potential limitation of the present study is that the response rate and the remission does not necessarily correspond to a first intent to treat these patients, as being referred by their GP, some of them may have been treated before with another AD.

title: Pharmacological management of alcohol dependence in chronic schizophrenia
abstract: Background: Patients with schizophrenia have a 50% rate of cooccuring substance use disorder including alcohol use, and the comorbid substance abuse has a markedly negative impact over the course of schizophrenia [1]. Cases of psychotic spectrum disorder had worse alcohol outcomes than those without such a disorder and a better prognosis when receiving active medication (disulfiram, naltrexone or a combination of the two) than when receiving placebo [2]. A recent literature review detected a considerable gap in the research data available to inform evidence-based practice in schizophrenia with comorbid substance use disorder [3]. Objective: To assess the efficacy of pharmacological management of alcohol dependence in chronic schizophrenia, using disulfiram or naltrexone. Methods: A group of 20 patients, 11 female and 9 male, mean age 40.2, diagnosed with chronic schizophrenia and alcohol dependence, according DSM IV TR criteria, were randomly, openlabel distributed in 2 parallel groups with patients receiving either disulfiram 250 mg/day (n = 12) or naltrexone 50 mg/day (n = 8). Patients were stabilized on an antipsychotic medication during the last month previous to their admission in this study. Subjects were evaluated for psychotic symptoms severity, daily functioning and severity of dependence, using Positive and Negative Syndrome Scale (PANSS), Global Assessment of Functioning (GAF), Clinical Global Impressions - Severity (CGI-S) and Inventory of Drug Taking Situations-alcohol focused version (IDTS). These measurements were applied every week during the first month and every 4 weeks for another 5 months. Inclusion criteria: ability to sign informed consent, at least one caregiver involved in patient's behavior monitoring, IDTS score over 100, age between 18 and 65. Exclusion criteria: prior treatment with naltrexone or disulfiram, pregnancy test positive, active suicidal ideation or recent suicidal attempt, other comorbid axis I disorder or axis II pathology. Intent-to-treat-analysis and last-observation-carried-forward were used in the statistical processing of data. Results: At week 24, patients had a mean global improvement of the PANSS score of 26% reported to baseline, with no significant differences between groups. The IDTS score improved overall with 45.2 points to baseline (p>0.01), with greater improvements observed in areas like 'physical discomfort' (p = 0.003) and 'testing personal control' (p = 0.005). Intergroup differences were not significant regarding the IDTS scores (p = 0.144). CGI-S decreased from a mean value of 4.5 to 1.5 at week 20 and remained at the same value until the endpoint, without significant differences between groups. Mean GAF score increased with 45.2% at week 24 (p>0.001). A number of 5 patients discontinued treatment due to adverse events (vomiting, nausea, abdominal pains, n = 2) or non-compliance (n = 3), more in the disulfiram group (p>0.05). Mild and moderate adverse events were reported in 6 patients in the disulfiram treated patients vs. 4 such reports in the naltrexone group. Conclusions: Naltrexone is an efficient therapeutic option in patients with chronic schizophrenia with alcohol dependence and is better tolerated than disulfiram, which also proved itself efficient, but with a higher rate of discontinuation due to side effects.

title: Does outcome of acute pancreatitis differ with obesity classification?
abstract: Purpose: During recent decades, there has been a steady increase in the incidence of acute pancreatitis in North America and this increase has been paralleled by an increase in prevalence of obesity. Obesity is likely to increase the risk of local and systemic complications and possibly death in patients with acute pancreatitis. A meta-analysis revealed that obese individuals have increased risk of AP and develop significantly severe AP than compared with normal weight individuals. A prospective study showed that obesity represents a more severe AP and number and types of complications increase in categories of increasing BMI while another retrospective study contradicted the same. This is to note that none of these studies were conducted on American population. The purpose of this study is to determine whether there exists a relationship between Acute Pancreatitis (AP) outcome and Obesity as classified by World Health Organization. Methods: We retrospectively reviewed electronic medical records of patients who were admitted in The Medical Center of Central Georgia from Sept 2007 to Nov 2012 with confirmed Acute Pancreatitis according to Atlanta Classification. Causes of pancreatitis were divided in to three categories- alcoholic, biliary and other (non-alcoholic, non-biliary). We assessed if there was a difference in outcome of alcoholic and biliary pancreatitis according to BMI classification for length of stay, need for ICU management, surgical intervention, Charlson's Comorbidity Index, and mortality. Statistical analysis was performed using SAS version 9.3 (SAS Institute, Cary, NC). (Table Presented) Variables were analyzed using the Chi-Square test or Fisher's Exact test. Patient with age <18 years and pregnancy were excluded. Results: One patient with alcoholic pancreatitis expired and was classified as being underweight. There was no significant statistical difference in alcoholic group in different BMI categories for clinical outcomes as measured by length of stay >7 days (p=0.55), level of care (p=0.66), surgical intervention (p=0.27) and their Charlson's co-morbidity index (p=0.91). In biliary pancreatitis group, interestingly patient who were obese had shorter duration of stay in hospital. There was no statistical significance in this group in separate categories for level of care (p=0.69), surgical intervention (p=0.38) and Charlson's co-morbidity index (p=0.33). One normal BMI patient expired in this group. Conclusion: Interestingly, obese patients with biliary pancreatitis were found to have shorter duration of stay than their normal and overweight counterparts and there was no significant difference in clinical outcomes among different BMI categories in alcoholic pancreatitis.

title: Evaluation of current termination of pregnancy and related services at Grimsby (UK) and recommendations for service improvement
abstract: Objective: To develop local termination of pregnancy (TOP) dataset and to identify "hotspots" for highest activity and gaps in our fertility control services. Methods: This was a retrospective analysis of 305 women who received TOP under section C of the Abortion Act 1967 over a period of 9 consecutive months from 1st March through to 31st October 2012. Results: There were 275 (90.2%) British White (BW) and 30 non-BW women. Among 30 non-BW women, 10 (3.3%) were British Asian, 8 (2.6%) were Polish, 6 (2.0%) were British Black or Black, 5 (1.6%) were Chinese and 1 (0.3%) was White Latvian. The TOP rate was 8.9% in the under 18 years old and 27.9% in the over 30 years old. Totally 240 TOPs (78.7%) occurred in <10 weeks and 276 TOPs (90.5%) occurred under 13 weeks of gestation. Eight-five women who received TOP-service have had one or more previous termination(s) in the last 3 years. The contraception use was low pre-TOP and none of the women were on long-acting reversible contraception (LARCs) pre-TOP, including those who had repeat terminations. Conclusion: There are inequalities and gaps in the TOP and related services in Grimsby which must be addressed to reduce the rate of TOP. This is a major challenge involving multiple agencies. Provision of contraception across all age and ethnic groups, improving sex education, engaging with parents and women to improve their negotiation skills for safer sex, supporting vulnerable women, reducing risk factors e.g. alcohol and substance misuse and raising aspirations across the region will contribute to a reduction in termination rate. © 2013 The Editorial Board of Journal of Reproduction and Contraception.

title: Characterising sleep apnoea syndrome in type 2 diabetes (Sweet Sleep study)
abstract: Background and aims: Sleep apnoea is highly prevalent in patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM). However, it is unknown whether or not diabetic patients share the same sleep breathing pattern than non-diabetic patients. Materials and methods: Case-control study between 119 T2DM patients and 238 non-diabetic subjects closely matched by age, gender, BMI, waist and neck circumferences, and smoking status. The exclusion criteria included chronic respiratory disease, neuromuscular and cerebrovascular disease, alcohol abuse, use of sedatives, and pregnancy. Examination included a respiratory polysomnography, oxygen saturation measures as the cumulative percentage of time spent with oxygen saturations below 90% (CT90), and the degree of sleepiness using the Epworth Sleepiness Scale (ESS). Studies with less than 5 hours of correct signal recording were ruled out. An apnoea was defined as cessation of airflow with duration of at least 10 seconds, and differentiation between obstructive and central apnoeas was made. The apnoeahypopnea index (AHI) was defined as the sum of apnoeas plus hypopneas divided by time in bed. Results: A higher AIH was observed in T2DM patients (34.0±3.4 vs. 26.0±2.8 events/hour; p=0.017). When sleep events were evaluated separately, a similar incidence of hypopnea events was present in diabetic and non-diabetic patients (18.3±1.1 vs. 16.7±3.9 e/h; p=0.951). However, in T2DM patients, a significantly increase in the number of apnoea events (15.2±8.2 vs. 10.3±3.2 e/h; p=0.048) and in the CT90 (18.0±33.5 vs. 10.7±10.4 %; p=0.042) were detected. No differences between obstructive and central apneas were observed. In addition, diabetic patients also showed higher daily sleepiness (7.5±3.6 vs 6.0±3.2, p=0.012) than non-diabetic subjects. Conclusion: T2DM adversely affects breathing during sleep, becoming an independent risk factor for higher rates of sleep apnoeas, as well as severe nocturnal hypoxemia and daily sleepiness.

title: Risk of spina bifida and maternal cigarette, alcohol, and coffee use during the first month of pregnancy.
abstract: This study was conducted to assess the association between the risks of spina bifida (SB) in relation to cigarette, alcohol, and caffeine consumption by women during the first month of pregnancy. Between 1988-2012, this multi-center case-control study interviewed mothers of 776 SB cases and 8,756 controls about pregnancy events and exposures. We evaluated cigarette smoking, frequency of alcohol drinking, and caffeine intake during the first lunar month of pregnancy in relation to SB risk. Logistic regression models were used to calculate adjusted odds ratios and 95% confidence intervals. Levels of cigarette smoking (1-9 and ≥10/day), alcohol intake (average ≥4 drinks/day) and caffeine intake (<1, 1, and ≥2 cups/day) were not likely to be associated with increased risk of SB. Further, results were similar among women who ingested less than the recommended amount of folic acid (400 μg/day).

title: Alcoholism and timing of separation in parents: Findings in a midwestern birth cohort
abstract: Objective: We examined history of alcoholism and occurrence and timing of separation in parents of a female twin cohort. Method: Parental separation (never-together; never-married cohabitants who separated; married who separated) was predicted from maternal and paternal alcoholism in 326 African ancestry (AA) and 1,849 European/ other ancestry (EA) families. Broad (single-informant, reported in abstract) and narrow (self-report or two-informant) measures of alcoholism were compared. Results: Parental separation was more common in families with parental alcoholism: By the time twins were 18 years of age, parents had separated in only 24% of EA families in which neither parent was alcoholic, contrasted with 58% of families in which only the father was (father-only), 61% of families in which only the mother was (mother-only), and 75% in which both parents were alcoholic (two-parent); corresponding AA percentages were 59%, 71%, 82%, and 86%, respectively. Maternal alcoholism was more common in EA never-together couples (mother-only: odds ratio [OR] = 5.95; two parent: OR = 3.69). In ever-together couples, alcoholism in either parent predicted elevated risk of separation, with half of EA relationships ending in separation within 12 years of twins' birth for father-only families, 9 years for mother-only families, and 4 years for both parents alcoholic; corresponding median survival times for AA couples were 9, 4, and 2 years, respectively. EA maternal alcoholism was especially strongly associated with separation in the early postnatal years (mother-only: birth-5 years, hazard ratio [HR] = 4.43; 6 years on, HR = 2.52; two-parent: HRs = 5.76, 3.68, respectively). Conclusions: Parental separation is a childhood environmental exposure that is more common in children of alcoholics, with timing of separation highly dependent on alcoholic parent gender.

title: Alcohol exposure in pregnancy and cognitive development at school age: A Brazilian longitudinal study
abstract: Alcohol consumption during pregnancy has been associated with changes in physical, neurological and behavioral of children, and the consequences on child development are widely varied in extension and severity. In Brazil, studies have shown that the prevalence of alcohol dependence in women is 5.7 % and approximately 22 % of women consume alcohol at risk levels to the fetus during pregnancy The damage caused by alcohol in the development of children depends on the pattern of maternal consumption, stage of gestation in which exposure to alcohol occurred in addition to other risk factors such as genetic factors, maternal and fetal metabolism, nutritional status of the mother, use of other drugs, health condition of the mother, maternal age and socioeconomic level. Studies have shown consistent evidence of association between heavy alcohol consumption during pregnancy and development of FAS, however results of studies on consumption levels low to moderate are still controversial This study evaluated the cognitive development of 86 school age children in relation to socio-demographical data and pattern of maternal alcohol consumption during gestation using Columbia Mental Maturity Scale (CMMS). Differences were observed among age deviation scores (ADS) above mean and higher maternal age (p = 0.01), higher birth weight (p = 0.05) and higher parity (p = 0.04). Analyzing the sample by gender, we observed lower mean scores in boys whose mothers used in days any quantity of alcohol during pregnancy higher than mean (p = 0.01) and also in those whose mothers used three or more doses of alcohol per occasion during pregnancy above mean (p<0.0001). Low/moderate alcohol use during pregnancy was associated to lower cognitive performance, particularly in boys. In summary, use moderate of alcohol during pregnancy was associated with lower cognitive performance in male children. Despite the effects of prenatal exposure to alcohol in children's cognitive development are widely documented, the data obtained so far have been controversial, especially with mild/ moderate alcohol exposure during pregnancy, possibly due to the different designs used and the complexity of the analysis the various factors pre-and postnatal-related outcomes. Controlled studies with a larger number of cases and the introduction of biological markers of alcohol exposure during pregnancy are required in order to enable an early detection of side effects, a better understanding of the severity and extent of damage in cognitive functions and identification of cognitive disorders that may be more affected by prenatal exposure to alcohol, providing an early intervention possible deficits found. In relation to maternal report on alcohol consumption during pregnancy, our results showed higher levels of consumption obtained from prospective data compared with the retrospective. In general, studies have considered the prospective data on prenatal exposure to alcohol more accurate and valid when compared to retrospective data because of recall bias.

title: Characterization of sleep apnea syndrome in type 2 diabetic patients (sweet sleep study)
abstract: There is growing evidence suggesting than sleep apnea is highly prevalent in patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM). However, whether diabetic patients share the same sleep breathing pattern than non-diabetic patients remains to be elucidated. For this purpose we designed a case-control study between 119 T2DM patients and 238 non-diabetic subjects closely matched by age, gender, BMI, waist and neck circumferences, and smoking status. The exclusion criteria included chronic respiratory disease, neuromuscular and cerebrovascular disease, alcohol abuse, use of sedatives, and pregnancy. Examination included a respiratory polysomnography, oxygen saturation measures as the cumulative percentage of time spent with oxygen saturations below 90% (CT90), and the degree of sleepiness using the Epworth Sleepiness Scale (ESS). Apnea was defined as cessation of airflow with duration of at least 10 seconds, and an accurate differentiation between obstructive and central apneas was performed. The apnea-hypopnea index (AHI) was defined as the sum of apneas plus hypopneas divided by time in bed. A higher AIH was observed in T2DM patients (34.5±9.3 vs. 26.2±8.1 events/hour; p=0.017). When apnea and hiponea were evaluated separately, a similar incidence of hypopneas events was present in diabetic and nondiabetic patients (18.3±4.2 vs. 16.7±5.3 e/h; p=0.951). By contrast, both the rate of apneas and CT90 were significantly increased in diabetic patients (15.2±2.8 vs. 10.3±1.9 e/h; p=0.048, and 18.0±6.7 vs. 10.3±7.7 %; p=0.042, respectively). No differences between the rate of obstructive and central apneas were observed. In addition, diabetic patients also showed higher daily sleepiness (7.5±3.1 vs 6.0±4.7, p=0.012) than non-diabetic subjects. In conclusion, T2DM patients have a higher rate of apneas than non-diabetic subjects, leading to more severe nocturnal hypoxemia and daily sleepiness.

title: Very premature child birth and early mother-infant relationship: the oLIMPE-EPIPAGE 2 cohort
abstract: Premature birth is a stressful experience affecting mother-infant interaction characteristics. Negative experiences just after the birth could have a significant and long-lasting influence on child outcome. The quality of the early mother-infant interaction is therefore considered as one of the multiple factors thatmay influence the prognosis of the very preterm babies. As part of EPIPAGE 2 (Etude Epidémiologique sur les Petits Ages Gestationnels) the 2nd French prospective population-based cohort study, OLIMPE (Observation Lien Mere Prématuré) considered for inclusion all singleton live births occurring from 24 to 32 completed weeks of gestation (WG) between May and December 2011 and hospitalised in 13 participating NICU from 9 French regions. A multidisciplinary network including neonatologists, psychiatrists, psychologists, psychomotor therapists and epidemiologists led this research. The main purpose was to explore the impact of the quality of the mother-child interactions on children outcome at 5 years of age, including behavioural and emotional development, communication, social integration and autonomy. Exclusion criteria were: severe neonatal complication, infant malformation, chromosomal abnormalities, maternal psychiatric illness and/or drug/alcohol abuse, and poor maternal French knowledge. To provide a standardized observation of mother-child interaction, the Massie Campbell scale (ADS Scale) was used. Two stages of observation were planned: at the end of the child hospitalisation and at 6 months of corrected age, by observing themother and child reaction during a routine paediatric examination. At 6 months, the social withdrawal behaviour of the child (ADBB: Alarm Distress Baby) was also observed. Maternal mental state was assessed with 3 self-rating questionnaires (Center for epidemiologic studies depression scale: CESD, State Trait Anxiety Inventory: STAI, Perinatal post traumatic stress questionnaire: PPQ). The ADS and ADBB scales required a training and calibration of the observers realized before the start of the inclusions and pursued regularly during all the study. Neonatal and obstetrics data aswell as information on child development will be extracted from EPIPAGE 2 database for the 172 dyads included. This project has a preventive dimension and we aimed to facilitate the detection of the high-risk dyads.

title: Recent alcohol and marijuana use as predictors of sexual risk outcomes over 18-months among african-american female adolescents
abstract: Few, if any, studies have explored patterns of alcohol and marijuana use as predictors of sexual risk exclusively among African-American female adolescents, who have disproportionate risk of adverse sexual health outcomes. The objective was to assess recent alcohol use, marijuana use and use of both substances as predictors of sexual risk outcomes during 18-months of follow-up among African- American female adolescents (14-20 years) assigned to the control arm of an HIV prevention trial. All participants, regardless of study condition, received an intervention demonstrated to decrease sexual risk behavior and sexually transmitted infections (STIs). Participants completed assessments at baseline and every 6 months. Generalized estimating equations compared sexual risk outcomes during follow-up among participants who in the 90 days prior to baseline assessment reported using only alcohol, only marijuana or both substances relative to individuals reporting using neither substance, controlling for baseline dierences and baseline measure of the outcome. Of 307 (86%) participants with follow-up data, 71 (23%) used only alcohol, 33 (11%) used onlymarijuana and 89 (29%) used both substances. Relative to recent use of neither substance at baseline, use of only alcoholmarginally predicted T. vaginalis acquisition (AOR: 2.08, 95%CI: 0.99, 4.33). Use of only marijuana predicted a reduced number of vaginal sex partners (B: -0.51, 95%CI: -0.99, -0.04) and reduced likelihood of condom use during the last vaginal sex act (AOR: 0.50, 95%CI: 0.28, 0.91). Use of both substances predicted sex with a partner recently released from incarceration (AOR: 2.17, 95%CI: 1.07, 4.39), pregnancy (AOR: 3.03, 95%CI: 1.06, 5.66) and incident T. vaginalis infection (AOR: 2.64, 95%CI: 1.45, 4.80). Recent substance use was common among this sample. Although participants received an ecacious STI/HIV prevention intervention, recent use of alcohol and/or marijuana predicted sexual risk during follow-up. Recent use of both alcohol andmarijuana predicted riskier sexual partners and adverse biological outcomes. STI/HIV and pregnancy prevention programs serving African-American female adolescents may benefit by assessing recent substance use, targeting services to recent marijuana and alcohol users and addressing the role of substance use on sexual risk. Researchers should seek to better understandmechanisms by which recent marijuana and alcohol use influence future sexual risk.

title: I'm fine, i've only had a little
abstract: Previous research has shown that after consuming alcohol women tend to perceive risky sexual situations as less risky or threatening than they may actually be (Davis et. al 2009, Testa et al 2000). Continuing research in this area is important in order to develop more eective strategies to prevent assault. The aim of our research was to conduct an experiment testing if even low levels of alcohol intoxication can have a significant impact on a woman's decision about whether or not to accept further drinks in risky situations. Specifically, we tried to assess a woman's risk analysis, judgment, and contributing factors of her decision to accept a drink in a series of sexually-risky scenarios. Our experiment was a double-blind within subject study of 12 drinking women (M age = 22.08, SD=1.5) who completed a total of 3 sessions each. The 3 sessions tested the 3 levels of the IV which were a low level alcohol condition (BAC = .04%), a placebo condition, and a water condition. Sessions were at least one week apart and beverage conditions were assigned in random order. At each session, after being given a breathalyzer and pregnancy test, participants were given the beverage (vodka tonics or water) for that session. Following a short absorption period, participants read 8 romantic scenarios in which the participant imagines she is in a particular scenario and is being pressured to drink by a man she finds attractive and interesting. The scenarios involve varying degrees of riskiness but all are risky. Each participant rated likelihood to drink and number of drinks she anticipated consuming in each scenario. We ran Analyses of Variance with RepeatedMeasures for bothmeasures for each scenario. For two scenarios, intoxicated participants rated themselves as more likely to accept another drink (p < .05). In four scenarios, intoxicated participants rated themselves as likely to drink significantlymore than when they were consuming placebo or water (p < .05). Furthermore, we used a compositemeasure of likelihood to drink and number of anticipated drinks and found that when participants were intoxicated to a .04 BAC, overall they reported increased likelihood to drink and a larger number of anticipated drinks (p < .05). Results suggest that even at this low level of alcohol consumption women may be more likely tomake the risky choice accepting another drink in an already risky situation.

title: Alcohol and hiv risk behaviors among childbearingwomen in st.Petersburg, russia
abstract: HIV transmission is a major health concern and research in countries with high rates of new infections is particularly important. Unlike the US where the number of cases attributed to heterosexual contact has stabilized, this number has continued to increase in Russia. There is minimal evidence to suggest what types of prevention approaches will be effective with general population. To date, limited gender specific data is available in Russia, with the majority of data being drawn from special populations (e.g., drug users and sexually transmitted disease clinic patients). Data on sexual behaviors and HIV risk in women in the general population are limited and the extent to which women's risky drinking patterns affect sexual behaviors and HIV risk in women in Russia remains unknown. This study is aimed at identifying the HIV risk and prevention needs among a sample of childbearing age women at risk for alcohol-exposed pregnancy (AEP) in Russia and answers the question about association between alcohol consumption and HIV risk in the general population. Sample and method: Women were recruited to complete an HIV risk survey from a sample of women who participated in a clinical trial evaluating a FASD prevention intervention in St. Petersburg, Russia. The study participants were recruited from city OB/GYN clinics as a women at risk for AEP. A total of 362 women completed the HIV risk survey in 2011-2012 and reported about their HIV risk behaviors, their partners' HIV risk and related questions. Results: In this sample, women who used alcohol before sex were more likely to report multiple sexual partners and less likely used condoms compared to women who did not use alcohol before sex. Women's reports indicated that a significant proportion of their partners were at risk for HIV because of multiple relationships, history of drug use or serving in prison.Women who were in a stable relationship with only partner did not perceive themselves as being at risk for HIV infection and did not use condoms or any other protection means despite of the lack of awareness about their partner's HIV status. Discussion: Prevention messages aimed at increasing condom use as protection against HIV/ STDs may not reach women who are in stable relationships. Additional research is needed to identify prevention strategies including increasing utilization of HIV testing.

title: Directional relationship between alcohol use and antisocial behavior during adolescence: Cross-lagged analysis of alspac data
abstract: A correlational relationship between alcohol (mis)use and antisocial behaviors has been well established, but consensus has not been reached regarding the directional relationship between the two: does alcohol use contribute to antisocial behavior, or does antisocial behavior lead to alcohol use? In this study, a cross-lagged model is used to examine the directional relationship between alcohol use and antisocial behavior with longitudinal data collected from adolescents at ages 13, 14, 15, and 18, from the Avon Longitudinal Study of Parents and Children (ALSPAC). ALSPAC is a prospective study on health and development that followed women in the Bristol area of the UK and their children from pregnancy onward. Because the items tomeasure alcohol use and antisocial behavior changed across time, we used an Item Response Theory approach linking common items across time to ensure equivalent scales ofmeasurement. Explorative factor analyses at each age indicated that single dimensionality could be reasonably assumed for both alcohol use and antisocial behavior. The levels of antisocial behavior rose up to age 15, dropped at age 18, and were consistently higher in men. The levels of alcohol use increased from age 13 to 18 without noticeable sex dierences. Latent variances of both alcohol use and antisocial behavior decreased over time. From the patterns of path coecients, we found: 1) preceding alcohol use and antisocial behavior were the strongest predictors of subsequent alcohol use and antisocial behavior; 2) cross-lagged paths indicated that the major direction of eect is fromearlier antisocial behavior to later alcohol use; and 3) sex dierences were found between 13 and 14 and between 15 and 18. Inmen only, antisocial behavior at 13 predicted alcohol use at 14, and alcohol use at 15 predicted antisocial behavior at 18. Our findings indicate that earlier in adolescence, antisocial behavior is predictive of subsequent alcohol use (but not vice versa), consistent with previous cross-lagged models, but mid to late adolescence, alcohol use is also predictive of subsequent antisocial behavior, inmen only.

title: Gender differences in drinking,mood symptoms and risk behaviors among HIV-infected outpatients inwestern kenya
abstract: Two-thirds of those with HIV worldwide live in sub-Saharan Africa. Alcohol use is associated with risky sex and poor adherence to antiretroviral medications. In western Kenya, hazardous drinking was reported by HIV-infected (53%) and general medicine (68%) outpatients. In this pilot study in western Kenya, data were derived from the baseline survey (n = 75) of HIV-infected outpatients who reported hazardous or binge drinking. Participants were enrolled in a trial of cognitive-behavioral therapy to reduce drinking (R21AA016884). The purpose of this study was to examine gender dierences in demographic and behavioral instruments, which were culturally and linguistically adapted. Results showed dierences in drinking,mood symptoms and risk behaviors. Women reported fewer years of education (M = 5.8, SD=3.9, women; M = 10.3, SD=3.0, men;p < .0001); and fewer were married (26.3%women, 89.2%men; p < .001) compared tomen. Fewer women had disclosed HIV to someone (52.6%women, 73%men).Women were significantly more depressed (PHQ-9 score ≥10, 50% women, 27%men;p < .05), and anxious (GAD-7 score ≥10, women 47.40%,men 21.6%;p < .05). Using the 30-day Timeline Followback, men reported significantly more drinking days (M = 8.0, SD=6.7, women;M = 12, SD=8.6, men;p < .05) and number of drinks per day (M = 4.3, SD=2.8, women; M = 7.1, SD-5.6, men;p < .01). There were no dierences in reported drinking of locally made spirits (chang'aa) in past 30 days (79%women, 73%men). Secondary to drinking, men and women reported similar levels of partner violence in past 30 days (44.7%women, 54%men) and expectations of enhanced sexual activity (M = 11.9, SD=11.1, women;M = 16, SD=11.2, men).More women than men reported never using condoms in their lifetime (42.1% women; 16.2%men). Women most commonly endorsed the reason of partner refusal (83.9% women; 34.4%men).Women more often endorsed engaging in higher risk professions: chang'aa brewer/barmaid/transactional sex (women 50%; men 13.5%). Regarding alcohol beliefs, slightly more women reported that alcohol oers general health benefits during pregnancy (65.8%women; 59.5%men). Together these pilot results suggest high-risk behaviors are reported by both Kenyan HIV-infected men and women. Women drink less, report worse mood and less HIV disclosure and more high-risk employment compared to men.Men report substantially heavier drinking behavior. More research in a larger sample is needed including assessment of high risk sexual behaviors.

title: Differences inmeg gamma band activity during performance of a prosaccade task in adolescentswith FASD
abstract: Fetal alcohol spectrum disorders (FASD) are characterized by a broad spectrum of behavioral and cognitive consequences that impact the long-term quality of life for individuals with FASD. However, the changes in the underlying brain structure and function that cause these behavioral and cognitive impairments are not well understood. Previous studies have identified dose dependent eects in behavioral performance of pro- and anti-saccade tasks in children with FASD. In this study, we focus on elucidating the cortical network responsible for initiating the visual saccades in a prosaccade task. Using the Elekta Neuromag 306 channel system, we collected MEG data from 15 adolescents with FASD and 20 age-matched healthy controls (HC). The participants were 12 to 20 years old (mean 15.9± 0.4 years). During the prosaccade task the participants began each trial by gazing at the centrally placed fixation point. After a variable delay, a peripheral target appeared along the horizontal meridian in the left or right visual field. The participants were instructed to saccade to the target location as quickly and accurately as possible. Eye movement was recorded and synchronized to the MEG data using the SR Research Eyelink 1000 eye-tracker system. MEG data across participants were corrected for head movement and registered to a common head position to allow for sensorbased comparisons. The MEG data were averaged relative to the onset of the saccade as identified by the eye-tracker system. Time frequency analysis was performed using Fieldtrip to capture the activity responsible for initiating the saccadic response. After accounting for multiple comparisons, we identified 6 clusters over left and right frontal, parietal and occipital cortex, with significantly dierent amplitude in the gamma band (30-50 Hz) between FASD and HC participants during left target presentation. Furthermore, one cluster ∼250ms prior to the saccade onset located over right parietal cortex was significantly greater in HC versus FASD; yet only the FASD amplitude was correlated with saccadic reaction time (SRT; r = -0.67, p = 0.007). Although there was not a significant group difference (FASD vs. HC) in behavioral SRT, this dierence as measured by MEG suggests that gamma band activity is important for ecient initiation of the visual saccade with a specific impairment in individuals with FASD.

title: Using a cumulative checklist of alcohol-related dysmorphia in a clinic sample
abstract: Since the first identification of the hallmark facial characteristics associated with Fetal Alcohol Syndrome, there has been debate about how best to characterize the dysmorphia for purposes of consistent and reliable identification of the disorder for clinical and research purposes. For over 15 years, the Fetal Alcohol and Drug Exposure Clinic has been using a cumulative dysmorphia checklist with the sentinel features deferentially weighted. The checklist was adapted froma typical genetic dysmorphia checklist and a threshold score was established using a prospective sample of participants who were either exposed or non-exposed to prenatal alcohol.One disadvantage of the existing scoring format was that growth eects were incorporated into the checklist, making it dicult to independently assess the dysmorphology and the growth retardation of prenatal alcohol exposure. The current study uses an archival clinical database (n=988) that includes consecutive dysmorphia assessments collected from 1998 through 2006 to establish a new threshold that is independent of the growth eects. In the current study, we compared the new cumulative checklist score to the original cumulative checklist score across the entire clinic sample and then relative to FASD diagnosis, gender, and race. Percent agreement with the old threshold score was evaluated relative to alternatives for the new threshold scores. The new threshold scores were also evaluated relative to diagnostic systems that use only the three sentinel features (epicanthal folds, palpebral fissures, and hypoplastic philtrum).Within the clinic sample, the new dysmorphia score has amean of 10.4 (std=6.3) as compared to the mean of the old dysmorphia score, which was 12.7 (std=8.3) and was positively correlated with the old score (r=.91, p < .000). Both the new (r=-.249, p < .000) and old dysmorphia (r= -.231, p < .000) scores were negatively associated with age. Among those diagnosed with FAS, 91%were identified using a threshold of 8 and 86%were identified using a threshold of 9 on the new dysmorphia cumulative checklist. Sensitivity and specificity of the new threshold values relative to the old scoring method were also evaluated. The new cumulative dysmorphia checklist score provides a valid method of assessing the facial and other musculoskeletal anomalies often seen in individuals with a history of prenatal alcohol exposure independent of the growth eects of the exposure.

title: Inadequate intake of nutrients essential for neurodevelopment in children with FASD
abstract: This study evaluated dietary intake in children with fetal alcohol spectrum disorders (FASD). Pre-clinical research suggests that nutrient supplementationmay be able to attenuate cognitive and behavioral deficits in FASD. Currently, the rates of suciency/insuciency for essential nutrients in children with FASD are not known. These dietary data were collected as part of a randomized, double-blind controlled trial of choline supplementation in FASD. Pilot data examining the associations between changes in serum choline levels and neurodevelopmental changes are also presented. Participants included 20 children with FASD, ages 2.5 - 5 years, who were in a 9-month study of choline supplementation. The Automated Self-Administered 24-hour Recall system was given at baseline and at three month intervals. Dietary intake of macronutrients and 16 vitamins and minerals from food were averaged across the four data collection points. Nutrient totals were compared to national dietary intake data of children ages 2 - 5 years (What we Eat in America, NHANES 2009-2010). Totals were also compared to the Recommended Dietary Allowances/Adequate Intakes (RDA/AI). Serum choline levels andMullen Early Learning Scale scores were available in a subsample (n=12) at baseline and study completion. Compared to the dietary intakes of children in the US, children with FASD had lower intakes of calcium, p<.001, riboflavin, p=.013, vitamin B6, p=.036, vitamin D, p<.001, and choline, p=.002. Based on the RDA/AI, children with FASD had inadequate intakes of calcium (80%). Change in serumcholine from baseline to study completion was positively associated with improvements on the Mullen Early Learning Composite, r=0.62, p=.033, and the Fine Motor subscale, r=0.75, p=.005. In conclusion, children with FASD had lower intakes than children in the general population for 6 of the 16 vitamins and minerals examined. Inadequate intake was common for choline, vitamin D, and n-3 PUFAs, nutrients which have been shown in animal models to potentially attenuate the cognitive deficits of FASD. Additionally, we found associations between changes in serum choline and changes in global cognitive status, a finding which further emphasizes nutritional interventions as a potential treatment for the cognitive deficits in children with FASD.

title: The effects of choline supplementation on the vulnerability of lamb cerebellar purkinje cells in response to 1st trimester binge alcohol exposure
abstract: HumanMRI and autopsy studies reveal abnormal cerebellar development in children exposed to alcohol prenatally, irrespective of the period of exposure. Despite such known adverse eects, alcohol abuse during pregnancy remains a public health problem,making it necessary to identify methods to reduce the damaging eects of alcohol. One potential intervention is prenatal supplementation with choline. It has been previously reported that pre- and perinatal choline supplementation in animal models has mitigated alcohol's eects on spatial learning and has improved neuronal plasticity. In the sheep model, where all three trimester-equivalents of human brain development occur in utero, the cerebellum is vulnerable to prenatal alcohol exposure during all trimesters.We hypothesized that in the sheep model, choline supplementation would amelioratePurkinje cell loss induced by binge alcohol exposure. Two doses of alcohol were tested and a dietary supplement of choline (10 mg/kg) or a vegetable oil placebo was added to the feed from gestation day (GD) 4-133. Ewes were divided into 7 groups: low alcohol (1.75 g/kg dose)+choline, highalcohol (3.0 g/kg dose)+choline, low alcohol+ placebo, high alcohol+placebo, saline+choline, saline+placebo and normal control. Alcohol infusions mimicked a human binge pattern of drinking, 3 consecutive days of infusions per week followed by 4 days o. Infusions were given from GD 4- 42 (1st trimester-equivalent). Cerebella were harvested from lambs on post-natal day 150 and processed for stereological cell counting. Alcohol exposure induced significant decreases in Purkinje cell density and number in both the low and high dose groups (p < 0.05). There was an overall protective eect of choline supplementation on Purkinje cell density in the combined alcohol+choline group compared to the alcohol exposed group (p = 0.047). Consistent with our previous work, cerebellar Purkinje cells are vulnerable to alcoholinduced cell loss from both doses during the 1st trimester-equivalent of gestation and these deficits persist in postnatal life. Gestational choline treatment significantly protected against this loss, confirming its potential as an intervention to mitigate the neurodevelopmental defects resulting from prenatal alcohol exposure.

title: Gestational choline supplementation ameliorates t-maze reversal learning deficits inweanling lambs induced by first trimester binge alcohol exposure
abstract: In rodent models of fetal alcohol spectrum disorders (FASD), cognitive deficits are implicated in impaired T-maze spatial reversal learning. Recent studies with rats have indicated that supplemental administration of choline during or after the developmental period of alcohol exposure can ameliorate spatial reversal deficits, suggesting that prenatal choline supplementationmight be an eective intervention for cognitive deficits in FASD. This study tested whether the therapeutic potential of prenatal choline supplementation could be confirmed in a sheep model of binge exposure in the first trimester equivalent. Two hypotheses were tested: 1) alcohol exposure would produce deficits in reversal of a T-maze position discrimination; and, 2) gestational dietary supplementation of choline would ameliorate those deficits. Mated ewes were assigned either to a first-trimester ethanol (E) group, a saline (S) group or a normal control (NC) group. Group E received intravenous infusions of alcohol (2.5 g/ kg per day; 40%w/v) in a weekly binge pattern (3 consecutive days of infusions followed by 4 nontreatment days each week) beginning on gestational day (GD) 4 and ending on GD 42. Group S was given infusions of 0.9%saline. Ewes of the E and S groups were assigned either to receive a dietary supplement of choline (CH) (10 mg/kg) or vegetable oil placebo (P) in their feed from GD 4 through GD 133. This yielded 5 treatment groups: NC (n = 15), E/P (n = 14), E/CH (n = 10), S/P (n = 6), and S/CH (n = 12). T-maze training began at 12 weeks of age, with daily sessions occurring 5 days/ week. Lambs were given 5 days of habituation training, followed by 5 days of position discrimination training (3 trials per daily session, intertrial interval of 3 hours, reinforced side randomly assigned across subjects). Lambs were then given 10 days of training on the reversal task. There were no group dierences in acquisition of the position habit. During reversal, significant deficits were evident in the E/P group relative to the NC and S/P groups [F(2,32)=3.511, p = 0.042]. Group E/CH showed significantly improved reversal performance relative to Group E/P [choline X day interaction, F (9,198)=2.30, p = 0.018], and the E/CH group did not dier significantly from controls. These results suggest thatmaternal dietary choline supplementation can ameliorate or prevent some of the cognitive impairments that may be linked to executive function in FASD.

title: Acute heavy alcohol exposureon gestation day 8 fails todisruptmorris water maze spatial learning and memory in adult c57bl/6j mice
abstract: Fetal alcohol spectrum disorders (FASD) result from gestational alcohol exposure and can include neuroanatomical abnormalities and cognitive and behavioral dysfunction. Currently there are no treatments for the adverse outcomes in children with FASD. Two activity-dependent neuropeptides [NAPVSIPQ (NAP) and SALLRSIPA (SAL)] have been shown to prevent alcohol-induced fetal demise, growth restrictions and postnatal spatial learning deficits in C57BL/6 mice when administered 30 minutes before a 5.8 g/kg dose of alcohol administered via a single intraperitoneal (i.p.) injection on gestational day 8 (GD8). A recent report by Incerti et al. (2011) using this samemodel indicated that oral NAP and SAL treatment just prior to and during Morris water maze training (40- 49 days old) rescued spatial learning deficits. The goal of this study was to determine whether orally administered D-NAP and D-SAL could rescue spatial learning deficits in alcohol-aected adult ospring in a related mousemodel of heavy binge alcohol exposure, in which the 5.8 g/kg dose on GD8 is separated into two i.p injections of 2.9 g/kg alcohol (23.7%v/v in normal Ringer's solution) or Ringer's vehicle control, four hours apart (Sulik et al., 1981). Thismodel was chosen because it has been shown to produce significant volumetric reductions in the hippocampus, a brain structure critical to spatial learning and memory, while reducing the incidence fetal demise. Beginning on PD 67, mice were given daily gavage treatments with either the peptide treatment (40 lg D-NAPand 40 lg DSAL), or vehicle. On PD70, animals were given 7 consecutive days place training in the Morris water maze (water temperature 25°C). Each training session involved four acquisition trials, in which each mouse was given up to 60 sec to find a 9-cmdiameter escape platform submerged in the same location on every trial. Trials were separated by ∼3 minutes. A 60-sec probe trial was given after the last training trial, in which the platform was removed and search strategy examined. Computer-based video tracking collected path length data during each trial. Gestational alcohol exposure had no significant eect on acquisition of place learning, and peptide treatment did not significantly alter place learning in either treatment group. This contrasts with the significant deficits found by Incerti et al. (2011), suggesting the two prenatal binge models may yield dierent behavioral outcomes.

title: Dimethoxybenzylidene (DMXB) reduces balance deficits following “3rd trimester” ethanol exposure in female but not male rats
abstract: Ethanol (ETOH) exposure during prenatal development can have serious consequences for the central nervous system, including the cerebellum. The present study examined whether the alpha-7-nicotinic- acetylcholine-receptor (a7nAChR) agonist, DMXB, could reduce the eects of ETOH exposure during the “3rd trimester brain growth spurt” in rats. DMXB has been shown to reduce ETOH induced neurotoxicity in primary hippocampal cultures. ETOH (6 g/kg/day) was administered on postnatal days (PND) 1-7 as amodel for the “human 3rd trimester brain growth spurt.” Intubated and non-intubated control groups were also included. On PND 8, twenty-four hours after the last ETOH treatment, pups received an injection of DMXB (10 mg/kg) or saline. After weaning, subjects were tested on a single dowel rod on PNDs 31-33. On day 1 of testing, the rat was placed on the rod and allowed to enter an escape box. The distance was increased by 13 cm after each successful trial and this was the dependent measure. A failure was defined as falling o the dowel or two legs slipping o the dowel. To avoid fatigue, rats received three trials/day for three days. Female rats neonatally treated with ETOH showed deficits on this balance task but the ETOH exposed females treated with DMXB performed at similar levels as controls.Male rats did not demonstrate similar patterns of performance as the females. These results illustrate the possibe neuroprotective eects of DMXB on systems critical to balance deficits in female rats. This study also suggests that there may be sex dierences in sensitivity to ETOH and/or DMXB on thismotor task. Further research is necessary to determine whether DMXB can be beneficial in other behavioral paradigms as well as better the understanding of the underlyingmechanisms of its neuroprotective properties and its dierential eects on sex.

title: Effectsof ethanol exposure in adolescence on attention, impulsivity, aggression and anxiety-like behavior in adult wistar rats
abstract: Alcohol is a widely used drug among youth and associated with risky behaviors.However, to isolate the long-term eects of alcohol in humans from other environmental variables. Animal models provide a useful alternative for studying the mechanisms of dependence and cognitive-behavioral deficits caused by repeated alcohol during adolescence. To investigate the eects of ethanol exposure in adolescent rats during adulthood. Three groups of male Wistar rats (mean weight 81.4 g, n = 120) were housed in groups of four until post-natal day 60 (P60). From days P30-P46 rats received one of three treatments: 3 g/kg of ethanol (15% v/v, PO, n = 48), 1.5 g / kg of ethanol (12.5%v/v, PO, n = 36), or water (n = 36) every 48 hours. After P60, the animals were trained on the 5-choice serial reaction time task (5CSRTT) and on a delay discounting task.We also assessed aggressive behavior and anxiety-like behaviors during adulthood. The 5-choice task detects food-reinforced responding to 1 sec visual stimuli displayed every 5 sec on five response holes until a steady baseline is observed. Then five test sessions were conducted with short stimulus durations (0.5 s and 0.25 s),manipulating the inter trial interval (ITI, 2s and 15s) in random order for each animal. The animals achieved stable base line responding in 89 days, with no dierences among treatment groups. In test sessions, when the ITI was 15s the group that received 3 g/kg showed lower accuracy (72.5%correct) than the others (81.9%correct in the 1.5 g/kg group and 83.4%in the water group). The latency of correct responses diered significantly between groups, with the 1.5 g/kg group significantly higher than the 3 g/kg group (p < 0.05). There was no treatment group eect or group x session type interaction in the other measures.With respect to impulsivity, the animals treated with 1.5 g/kg alcohol were more impulsive than controls (i.e. tolerated only shorter delays). And the animals treated with the same concentration of alcohol were more aggressive (i.e. increased number of attack bites and threats, shorter attack latency) and had no eects on anxiety-like behaviors in the EPM as compared to control group. Intermittent exposure to alcohol during adolescence led to impaired performance on an attention task in adulthood andmay have compromised the readiness to respond, and the adult animals were more impulsive and aggressive.

title: Reasons for rejection of blood group matched prospective live liver donors in a high volume centre
abstract: Methods: Our donor assessment protocol consisted of selecting 18-55 years blood group matched, relatives, followed by a 4-phase evaluation. Phase 1 consisted of tests for systemic function, viral serology, screening for hepatic steatosis bv CT scan +/- liver biopsy. Those with liver attenuation index (LAI) <0 were rejected, 0-5 underwent a liver biopsy and >5 were accepted. Upper limits or acceptable steatosis for right and left lobe donation were 20% and 30% respectively. Phase 2: CT scan for vascular anatomy, volumetry, MRCP: Phase 3: Systemic evaluation. Phase 4: Systemic clearances and legal committee. Liver biopsy is done after volumes are acceptable. The study cohort included donors evaluated during February 2011 to October 2012. Results: 742 pre-screened living related live donors were evaluated for 407 LRLT including 3 dual lobe LRLT. Of these. 332 (44.74%) were rejected 60.8% during phase 1,23.4% during phase 2 and 15.6% during phases 3 and 4. Among the causes for rejection, steatosis/other abnormal features on liver biopsy were the commonest, accounting for 58.73 % (195/332). Of these, 47.2 % had LAI<0 and 3.6% had excessive steatosis on liver biopsy. 1.5% each were not accepted due to high BMI and fatty infiltration on CT and 2% due to abnormally high cholesterol. Additionally, biopsy done to look for steatosis revealed 1.5% had inflammation and 2.7 % had fibrosis. 20% were rejected due to inadequate graft (9.5%) or remnant (10.5%) volumes. 10% prospective donors backed out due to social/psychological reasons after they were medically suitable. 2.1 % were rejected due to HBsAg positivity, 1.8% due to variant anatomy; 1.2% due to cystic lesions on CT. 0.9% each were rejected by pulmonology, psychiatry, endocrinology, urology, neurology and the legal committee. 0.6% each were rejected due to CLD on CT scan, high cardiac risk, chronic alcoholism, and suspicion of thyroid and breast tumours. 0.3% of the rejections were due to pregnancy and dengue infection during evaluation. Conclusion: Nearly half the pre-screened prospective donors are rejected during evaluation. In our experience, the commonest reasons for rejection are NAFLD, inadequate projected liver volumes and psychological inability to accept donation. Rejection due to anatomical anomalies is rare.

title: Smoking and alcohol use in pregnancy: Prevelance in west Crete, Greece
abstract: Introduction/Background Maternal smoking and alcohol consumption during pregnancy are considered to be two of the most preventable and avoidable causes that may impair homeostasis and normal development of the fetus. They are associated with short-term and long-term adverse effects on child's health. Data on the prevalence of smoking and alcohol use in pregnancy is limited in Greece. This study aims to assess the prevalence of smoking and alcohol use in pregnant women, in a province of west Crete (Chania) that could be a representative sample of the Greek territory. Patients, Methods This is a prospective study that included mothers of babies born in the General Hospital of Chania the period from June 2011 to September 2012. An anonymous questionnaire survey about their smoking and alcohol habits as well as their age, ethnicity, educational level and annual income was conducted. Results 511 out of 600 mothers, selected randomly, answered the anonymous questionnaire. Mothers of Greek origin were almost 68%. Most of the mothers were between 25 to 35 years old (64%). 30% were University graduated, 57% secondary and 13% primary level educated. The annual income for the majority of them (82%) was less than 20.000 Euros (47% less than 10000). Smoking rates before and during pregnancy were 34% and 19% respectively. The majority of mothers (12.5%) continued smoking throughout pregnancy 5 to 10 cigarettes per day. Greek women were more often smokers compared with those of non-Greek origin (21% vs 14%). Higher smoking rates were recorded in the group of younger age, 18 to 20 years old (24%), in primary educated mothers (27%) with lower annual incomes (24%), but also, in discordance with the literature, in mothers with relatively high annual incomes (25.000 to 30.000 Euros) (35%). Notably, in a percentage of 14% of smoker mothers there was at least another smoker at home. Alcohol consumption rate during pregnancy was 20%. The majority used to drink alcohol throughout pregnancy (13.5%) and fewer than half of them used to consume from one drink per day (1.2%) to one drink per week (7.3%). The most preferable drinks were beer (9%) and wine (7%) or both (3.4%). Greek pregnant women consumed more frequently alcohol than non-Greeks (22% vs 16%). In accordance to the literature, higher rates were recorded in groups of older age (30 to 35 years old 23%, 35 to 40 years old 22% and more than 40 years old 28.6%), in university graduates (25%) and in the group of higher annual incomes (more than 30.000 Euros) (50%). Furthermore, 5% of mothers combined both, smoking and consuming alcohol during pregnancy. Conclusion Smoking rate during pregnancy in west Crete was of the highest among those recorded in Europe while alcohol consumption rate was near the lowest average. Interventions by obstetricians, pediatricians, midwives and health facilities targeting in reducing smoking and alcohol consumption during pregnancy are imperative.

title: Risk-associated behaviour in multiple sclerosis: A case control study
abstract: Objective: It is generally accepted that individuals who subsequently develop MS are more likely to be smokers, have suffered glandular fever and to have a low blood vitamin D level. Previous research suggested that a unifying premise is risk-associated behavior before MS onset. This survey explores several health-adverse behaviors using a case-control design. Methods: A questionnaire was completed by 94 patients with clinically definite MS. Their responses were compared to a control group of 59 who were patients with benign headache. Questions explored pre-symptomatic experience of: (a) alcohol, smoking, substance abuse, glandular fever; (b) contraceptive measures; (c) blood transfusion; (d) hazardous sport, gambling (e) sexual history, gynecologic infection, number of pregnancies, terminations of pregnancy. Data were adjusted for age of first symptoms and gender. Results: Compared to the headache group, MS subjects showed significant differences prior to symptom onset, adjusted for age of first symptoms and gender as follows: (a) consumption of alcoholic drinks (p = 0.004), and at an earlier age (p = 0.009) (b) smoked cigarettes (p = 0.028); and to have smoked more (p = 0.001); (c) reported a history of glandular fever/infectious mononucleosis (p = 0.035); (d) consumed recreational drugs (p = 0.007) notably cannabis (p = 0.005); (e) used a car seat belt (p = 0.008); (f) attended all-night parties (p = 0.014); (g) sunbathed (p = 0.027); (h) gambled on lottery (p = 0.037); (i) had more sexual partners (p<0.001) more pregnancies (p = 0.005) and at least one termination of pregnancy (p = 0.026). Conclusion: All but one variable (use of car seat belt) supports our hypothesis that MS subjects lead a riskier lifestyle prior to symptom onset. The most striking findings were for smoking, alcohol and glandular fever as confirmed by others. Novel associations were found for recreational drug use; attending all-night parties; gambling on the lottery; more sexual partners, more pregnancies and at least one termination of pregnancy. Such behavior during the MS prodrome may expose an individual to a variety of hostile environmental agents. The temptation to assign or explain on a causal basis, all statistically significant associations with later-developing MS should be avoided. These associations may simply reflect a particular pattern of living.

title: Targeted information on methotrexate and lifting alcohol restrictions in patients with RA and psa is safe and reduces patients' negative beliefs
abstract: Background Research regarding potential interaction between use of Methotrexate (MTX) and alcohol consumption is sparse (1-2, 5). Nevertheless patients traditionally are advised against alcohol intake while on MTX for safety reasons. Furthermore MTX generally is perceived by doctors and patients as a cytotoxic agent. Thus patients often associate the drug to cancer treatment and thereby resent the treatment. However, the doses used in the treatment of arthritis of <= 25 mg weekly only exerts anti-inflammatory effects. Recently the British society of Rheumatology has lifted their restrictions on alcohol intake (3) and one study found no evidence of increased liver toxicity accordingly (4). We present the results of a prospective single centre questionnaire study with one year follow up on the effects of an altered information strategy stressing the anti-inflammatory effects of MTX and lifting alcohol restrictions asking patients to adhere to national Danish guidelines (5). Objectives To investigate the effects of altered information strategy and the safety of increased alcohol limits for patients with Rheumatoid Arthritis and Psoriatic Arthritis. Methods Patients in a single outpatient clinic receiving MTX for Rheumatoid Arthritis or Psoriatic Arthritis were interviewed by postal delivered questionnaire for their beliefs regarding MTX and their alcohol consumption (6). Informed consent was obtained. The patients were on stable treatment for at least 6 months prior to answering the questionnaire. Liver enzyme levels the preceding year were gathered. A new information leaflet stressing the anti-inflammatory effects of MTX and advising alcohol intake kept within national guidelines was sent to all responders. One year later a follow up questionnaire was sent and liver enzyme levels during the year of observation was collected. All data were entered into a database and analyzed with descriptive and non-parametric statistical analyses. Results 117/127 patients responded to the one year follow up questionnaire. 76% were women, and 24% men. 10 patients were lost to follow up due to various reasons. 105 patients were still on MTX while 12 had discontinued their treatment for reasons of lack of response, side effects or planned pregnancies. Average dose of MTX was 14.7 mg/14.3 mg weekly. Alcohol was used by 97.7% compared to 79.2% at baseline. 10.5 % of the patients indicated that they had increased their intake of alcohol after receiving the new guideline. The mean consumption increased from 3.7 units to 5.5 units weekly (p=0.002). 13 % occasionally exceeded the limit. 10 % of the patients had significantly elevated liver enzymes (2xULN) prior to the intervention, and 9.5 % a year after (p = 0.98). Only 22% of the patients felt bothered by alcohol restrictions compared to 47% at baseline (p= 0.01). 19 % of the patients developed a more positive view on MTX treatment.
